A1.justification: Both complete 13-page PDFs describe the same PASDF research. Their text, equations, tables, figures and supplementary sections A–D are available and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original PASDF benchmark evaluations, anomaly-repair results and ablation studies, including supplementary quantitative and qualitative results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original benchmark, repair and ablation results in the main text and supplementary material.

M1.justification: Sections 3.3–3.7 and Algorithm 1 retain the same pose alignment, SDF network, positional encoding, clamped L1 loss, top-K anomaly scoring and Marching Cubes repair procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate detection, localization and reconstruction-based repair on Real3D-AD and Anomaly-ShapeNet. The represented categories, input conditions and supplementary examples are unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within each comparison in Tables 1–3. Table 5 and supplementary Tables A–B retain the same BTF(FPFH), PatchCore(FPFH) and PatchCore(PointMAE) comparisons with and without PAM.

E3.justification: Sections 4.1–4.2 retain the same dataset sizes and splits, sampling, model configuration, 2,000-epoch training budget and evaluation procedures. O-AUROC, P-AUROC, Chamfer Distance and Earth Mover’s Distance remain the evaluation metrics.

E4.justification: Tables 4–6 retain the positional-encoding, PAM-transfer and component ablations. Figures 3–4 and supplementary Figures A–B and Tables A–B contain the same qualitative cases and detailed PAM analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The statistical reporting practice is unchanged.

E6.justification: All reported scores in Tables 1–6 and supplementary Tables A–B are unchanged. PASDF retains mean O-AUROC/P-AUROC of 0.802/0.745 on Real3D-AD and 0.900/0.897 on Anomaly-ShapeNet; qualitative findings also match.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and equations (1)–(17), including pose marginalization, alignment, SDF learning and supplementary distance formulas, are unchanged apart from typesetting. No theoretical assumption, derivation or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about continuous pose-invariant representation, unified anomaly detection and repair, and state-of-the-art benchmark performance.

C2.justification: The explanations of alignment and positional-encoding effects are unchanged. Section 5 retains the same limitations concerning alignment cost, the single-normal-class assumption and sensitivity to point-cloud quality.

D1.justification: Both versions disclose the same architecture, hyperparameters, query sampling, training budget and V100 hardware. Supplementary data-preparation instructions and the code-access statement are also unchanged.

R1.justification: The 40-entry bibliography and the discussion positioning PASDF against earlier detection, implicit-representation and repair methods are unchanged. Reference differences are limited to spacing.

P1.justification: v2 adds Xintao Chen to the author list, marks Bozhong Zheng and Jinye Gan as equal contributors, and adds a corresponding-author marker for Yingna Wu with explanatory footnotes. The scientific prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The revised author block and new first-page footnotes cause limited text reflow across columns and pages, alongside minor typesetting differences. Figures, tables, captions and their substantive display structures are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 updates attribution and slightly reflows the presentation, while preserving the methods, experimental evidence, reproducibility information and limitations, including the appendices. These editorial changes do not materially alter the paper’s evidential strength or readability.
